answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the raven protocol requires nodes to deposit stake and undergo game-theoretic multi-agent auditing. Graph auditing checks topological cut verifications across the trust graph: if an entity tries to mirror identities to artificially inflate influence, any detected flow delta triggers stake slashing. Because sparse cut capacity imposes a superlinear attacker cost relative to swarm size, forging fake agents becomes mathematically unprofitable.
